title: Memorization capacity of deep ReLU neural networks characterized by width and depth
abstract: arXiv:2603.09589v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper studies the memorization capacity of deep neural networks with ReLU activation. Specifically, we investigate the minimal size of such networks to memorize any $N$ data points in the unit ball with pairwise separation distance $\delta$ and labels from a finite set of size $C$. Most prior studies characterize the memorization capacity by the number of parameters or neurons. We extend these results by constructing ReLU networks with adjustable width $W$ and depth $L$ satisfying $W^2L^2\log W=\mathcal{O}(N(\log(\delta^{-1})+\log C))$ that can memorize any such dataset. We also establish width-depth lower bounds that depend explicitly on $\delta$ and $C$ for networks capable of memorizing all such datasets. When $\log(\delta^{-1})\asymp\log N$, our construction achieves $W^2L^2\asymp N$ for suitable choices of width and depth. translated_title: 以宽度和深度刻画深度ReLU神经网络的记忆容量
translated_abstract: 本文研究了具有ReLU激活函数的深度神经网络的记忆容量。具体而言，我们研究了此类网络记忆任意 $N$ 个数据点（位于单位球内、两两间距为 $\delta$、标签来自大小为 $C$ 的有限集合）所需的最小网络规模。以往的大多数研究通过参数数量或神经元数量来刻画记忆容量。我们通过构造具有可调宽度 $W$ 和深度 $L$ 的ReLU网络扩展了这些结果，在满足 $W^2L^2\log W=\mathcal{O}(N(\log(\delta^{-1})+\log C))$ 的条件下，该网络可以记忆任何此类数据集。我们还建立了显式依赖于 $\delta$ 和 $C$ 的宽度-深度下界，适用于能够记忆所有此类数据集的网络。当 $\log(\delta^{-1})\asymp\log N$ 时，我们的构造在合适的宽度和深度选择下可达到 $W^2L^2\asymp N$。若 $\log C\asymp\log N$，则该阶数是最优的；若 $\log C=o(\log N)$，则该阶数在相差对数因子的意义下是最优的。
tldr: 本文突破了以往仅用参数或神经元数量刻画记忆容量的做法，通过同时调节宽度与深度构造ReLU网络，证明满足 $W^2L^2\log W=\mathcal{O}(N(\log(\delta^{-1})+\log C))$ 即可记忆任意数据集，并给出显式依赖数据间距与类别数的宽度-深度下界，在典型情形下达到 $W^2L^2\asymp N$ 的最优规模。
en_tdlr: This paper extends prior memorization capacity results by constructing ReLU networks with tunable width $W$ and depth $L$ that can memorize any dataset when $W^2L^2\log W=\mathcal{O}(N(\log(\delta^{-1})+\log C))$, establishes explicit width-depth lower bounds depending on data separation $\delta$ and class count $C$, and shows that $W^2L^2\asymp N$ is optimal (up to logarithmic factors) in typical regimes.
